chunks: 33 - Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah informed us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Isa narrated to us, he said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Bata'i narrated to us, from his father, from al-Mufaddhal, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying:

The master of this matter will have a house called the House of Praise, in which there is a lamp that shines from the day he was born until the day he rises with the sword, which will not be extinguished.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Matter (referring to the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the House of Praise and its lamp in the context of the Mahdi?
ai.summary: In al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq identifies the 'House of Praise' (Bayt al-Hamd) as the specific dwelling of the Mahdi, featuring a perpetual lamp symbolizing his divine light from birth to his final emergence with the sword. This imagery underscores the continuity of the Imamate and the eschatological transition from occultation to visible authority, a key theme in Twelver Shia eschatology.
